title: Care, Human Enfeeblement, and the Existential Implications of AGI
abstract: arXiv:2611.14520v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Stuart Russell has named "human enfeeblement" as a long-term societal risk of advanced AI. This paper gives a new interpretation of the enfeeblement danger by interpreting it in light of recent work by Brian Christian, Alison Gopnik, and David Spivak on care and caregiving, and connecting it with the ontological design tradition of Terry Winograd and Fernando Flores. The enfeeblement that threatens is not merely a matter of cognitive off-loading and loss of knowledge, but a form of disengagement with the world which I explain in terms of an erosion of our capacities to care. This paper articulates a conception of care as a constellation of cultivable skills that involve us in the world and with each other, while making life worth living. Designing AI to support our capacities to care addresses the worry recently raised by Demis Hassabis and others regarding the questions of "meaning and purpose" that are looming in a post-AGI world.

translated_title: 关怀、人类衰弱化与AGI的存在论意涵
translated_abstract: 斯图尔特·罗素将“人类衰弱化”列为先进人工智能带来的一项长期社会风险。本文通过结合布莱恩·克里斯蒂安、艾莉森·戈普尼克和大卫·斯皮瓦克近期关于关怀与照护的研究，并将其与特里·温诺格拉德和费尔南多·弗洛雷斯的本体设计传统相联系，对衰弱化危险提出了新的诠释。所面临威胁的衰弱化不仅仅是认知外包与知识流失的问题，而是一种与世界脱节的形式，作者以我们关怀能力的衰退来解释这一点。本文阐明了一种关怀的构想，即将其视为一系列可培养的技能的组合，这些技能使我们投入世界之中并与他人相联结，同时使生活值得一过。设计能够支持我们关怀能力的AI，回应了德米斯·哈萨比斯等人近期提出的担忧，即后AGI世界中日益逼近的“意义与目的”问题。
tldr: 本文提出对AGI“人类衰弱化”风险的新诠释——真正的威胁不是认知外包而是人类关怀能力的衰退，因此应设计能够支持而非取代人类关怀能力的AI，以化解后AGI时代的意义与目的危机。
en_tdlr: This paper reinterprets the "human enfeeblement" risk of AGI as an erosion of our capacities to care rather than mere cognitive off-loading, arguing that AI should be designed to support these care capacities to address looming questions of meaning and purpose in a post-AGI world.
